title: On-call handoff draft - Harper Nelson
content:
Quick handoff notes / temp runbook (draft)

Summary (shift 11/07 -> 11/08)
- Lightweight shift. Pager noise low overall. Two alerts: one transient high-latency spike (resolved), one model-degraded-quality alert (ongoing).
- No SAC-level incidents. No customer escalations so far.
- Leaving behind temp procedures for model-fallback tests and KV-cache clearing steps (see below).

Current state / things to watch
- Model catalog: running rwd/open-7b-v2 as default for hosted-edge. Traffic stable.
- Autoscaler: healthy; average utilization 62% on dedicated pool us-west.
- Observability: some missing spans for streaming responses in the last 6h (tracing sampling flag flipped to 0.1 for debugging) - revert after 12h if not needed.
- Ongoing JIRA INC-987: degrade in response fidelity for open-7b-v2 on long-context prompts. Root cause suspected quantization mismatch during recent rollout.

Open incidents / tasks
- INC-987 (priority P2): degrade in fidelity. Work in progress. Assigned: Maya. Steps taken: rolled back auto-quantization profile to quant-v1 on canary nodes; running A/B evals. Next: run full eval set overnight and decide on full rollback.
- Tracing sampling change: temporary change made at 2024-11-07T21:10Z. Reminder to revert sampling to 0.5 by 2024-11-08T09:00Z unless asked otherwise.

Temporary procedures / quick playbook (use these if pager fires)
1) High overall API latency (pager: api-latency-sla)
   - Quick checks:
     * Check platform status dashboard: https://status.redwood.internal/ (login required)
     * Look at per-model p50/p95/p99 for last 5m in Console -> Model Metrics
     * Check autoscaler: kubectl get hpa -n dedicated (or use infra runbook)
   - Mitigation steps (fast):
     * If dedicated pool utilization > 80% and queue growing, scale up reserved nodes (infra-runbook can run: scripts/scale-dedicated.sh --region us-west --add 2).
     * If single model shows spike, temporarily route traffic to fallback variant (rwd/open-7b-v2 -> rwd/open-7b-v2-quant-safe). Update routing via console: Routes -> Edit -> add fallback rule.
   - Post-mortem checklist: collect logs (s3://redwood-logs/api/latency/YYYYMMDD), snapshot autoscaler events, gather sample requests that hit the spike.

2) OOMs on GPU workers (pager: gpu-ooms)
   - First step: identify recent pods with oomKilled (kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep OOMKilled).
   - If multiple pods impacted, temporarily reduce batch size limit via ModelConfig override: set token_batch_limit=64 for affected model. Use internal API: POST /internal/v1/models/<model>/override (auth via service account).
   - If still failing, cordon node, drain, and restart node (use infra helpers).

3) Degraded output quality / regressions (pager: model-quality-alert)
   - Quick triage:
     * Confirm metric: quality-regression-detector -> examples flagged count + severity.
     * Check recent rollout history for the model (Console -> Rollouts). Any new rollout in last 48h?
   - Mitigation (fast):
     * If rollout present, rollback to previous stable revision (Console -> Rollouts -> Rollback).
     * If no rollout, try switching traffic to a verified variant, or enable deterministic seed to reproduce sample failing cases.
   - Escalation: if rollback fails or multiple customers report, page NLP-eng (channel #nlp-oncall) and product-owner.

Temp procedure: KV cache clear (used during debugging of prefix mismatch)
- Why: rare cases of stale KV cache cause incorrect continuations on long conversations. Only do this when reproducing or as advised by ML-eng.
- Steps (careful):
  1) Identify affected shard(s) in Console -> Serving -> Shards.
  2) For each shard, run: curl -X POST https://internal-serving.redwood/api/v1/shards/<shard>/kv/cache/clear -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" (token from vault: secret/ops/oncall-token).
  3) Monitor traffic for errors; use canary first (pick 1 shard), wait 5m, then roll.

Notes to self / TODOs to finish this doc
- Add exact commands for scaling via infra CI job (need to copy from infra-runbook).
- Add sample curl with real internal token retrieval (vault path).
- Flesh out rollback play (screenshots of Console UI would help).
- Clean up links to Confluence page once INC postmortem is published.

Recent commands I ran (for debugging)
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=serving -c runner --since=2h | grep "latency spike"
- python infra/scripts/run_eval.py --model rwd/open-7b-v2 --evalset long-context --output /tmp/eval-open7b.txt
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/api/latency/20241107/ . --recursive

Quick contacts
- SRE oncall rotation: oncall-sre@redwood.internal (primary)
- NLP/Model eng: Maya Singh (maya@redwood.internal), Leo Garcia (leo@redwood.internal)
- Product owner (Hosted API): Priya Menon (priya@redwood.internal)
- Infra ops (scale help): Tom Huang (tom@redwood.internal)

Last words
- Low noise night so far. Main risk is INC-987 quality regression; please verify A/B eval results before doing a wide rollback. If you need help, ping Maya in #nlp-oncall or call my mobile.

-- Harper

Notes: this is a working draft; will move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/runbooks after vetting and screenshots added.
